events.description: While running in the hole with the mud hammer and 2 roller reamers, they got stuck for several hours and finally worked loose.
Running the mud hammer the third time also resulted in a failed run.
The CanRig system created discrepancies on the measurement of MSE and interfered with directional work to keep hole vertical.
Failed hammer run was indicated for the reason for the hammer failure.
Failed hammer run was indicated for the reason for the hammer failure.
The mud motor needed to be tested without the bit installed, and testing with the bit inside casing could cause damage.
Mud motors should have only new components or use only new mud motors due to hard and abrasive drilling conditions.
70% of our bit trips were due to lower bearing and housing failure, which also causes uncontrollable MSE due to higher torque and less differential.
The mud motor was found not to have been assembled with any new parts except for the lower bearings, limiting its operational hours.
Mud motors should be tested without the bit installed inside casing to avoid damage and ensure working conditions.

lessons_learned: Ensure that each mud motor is brand new, or if rebuilt, only new components are used to avoid failures and reduce bit trips.
Test mud motors without the bit installed inside casing to prevent damage and ensure working conditions.
Ream drilled sections every 2,000 ft to 3,000 ft of directional work using a conventional locked assembly to smooth out directional work and avoid getting stuck.
Avoid using CanRig surface oscillator while sliding to maintain hole verticality and ensure proper MSE reading.
If no losses are detected while drilling, do not use Sodium Silicate in cement slurry as it could lead to premature set of the cement slurry.
Obtain proper bottom hole temperature prior to casing to avoid issues with cementing operations.
